description: New York Paid Family Leave annual cap (ZP-TAX-US-2026-001 §13, test ID US-NY-PFL-001) -- proves the $411.91 annual maximum actually stops the contribution rather than letting the flat 0.432% run uncapped. The harness has no YTD/multi-period accumulator, so this uses one period high enough (monthly gross $10,000, i.e. $120,000/yr) that the UNCAPPED amount ($43.20/mo) already exceeds the capped monthly equivalent ($411.91/12 = $34.33/mo) within a single period -- a stricter proof of the same invariant the document's own CYTD-accumulation framing describes, not a literal replay of it.
source: ZP-TAX-US-2026-001 v1.0: Section 5 (NY Paid Family Leave: employee 0.432%, gross wages, annual employee max $411.91), Section 13 test US-NY-PFL-001 ("Stop employee contribution at $411.91"), Appendix A ("2026 employee contribution rate 0.432% with annual maximum $411.91"). Recomputed by running the real engine: uncapped 120000 * 0.432% / 12 = 43.20/mo; capped at 411.91/12 = 34.33/mo (rounded).
